recipes.name: Sausage Egg Muffins
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (4 ounce) can chopped green chile peppers, drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain.
Combine eggs, onion, and chile peppers in a large bowl. Add sausage, salt, and pepper; mix until well combined. Spoon 1/4 cup sausage mixture into each of the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until eggs are set and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage Egg Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These savory sausage and egg muffins are a nice alternative to the traditional breakfast sandwich. They're also perfect as an afternoon snack!

review.reviewBody: I tried this recipe and it came out pretty good. The only thing I will definitely add next time is more cheese. I also added some milk to the recipe to give it a fluffier consistency. Other than that, will try again. What I like most about this recipe is that it can be tweaked to my specifications, add bell pepper or mushroom, use bacon instead of sausage. I will keep in the recipe box for future use. Thanks!

I made these this morning but didn't have sausage so I made some with ham and cheese and some with peppers and onions. They were really good. I didn't read the directions carefully and filled the cups up to the top. It worked out fine and baked them for about 18 minutes. After reading the reviews I was nervous about them sticking so I buttered the cups and then sprayed them with butter flavored Pam. I also listened to the reviewer that said to take them out of the pan in about two minutes after taking them out of the oven. I took them out of the cups in a minute and a half and they came out very easily!! Will make again!

I followed advice from other reviewers and cut the eggs down to 10, added a cup of milk and a cup of shredded triple cheddar cheese. I skipped the onions, salt and pepper and replaced them with a teaspoon of Jane’s Krazy Mixed Up Salt, which is always amazing with eggs. I ended up with 2 dozen small muffins by filling the muffin cups up half way. They didn’t stick at all using silicone muffin pans + nonstick spray. The whole family loves them and we have a few left over for later. Will be making these regularly I think!

Very good! Took to work for a food day and received lots of compliments because of the taste and uniqueness. I kept the recipe the same except I used a greased mini muffin pan and placed items in as follows: 3/4 tsp sausage, topped with a good pinch of finely grated cheese, topped with the egg mixture (all other items mixed together with a 1/3 c. of milk). Baked for 13 minutes, removed from pan after cooled. I made them the night before, refrigerated in a plastic bowl with paper towels between layers. In the morning I layered these into my crockpot and turned it on warm - stayed moist and warm til they were gone! This made 48 minis -- we call them omelet poppers! Thanks for the recipe!

This is a good base recipe. Makes a bit more in my muffin tins - 6 eggs makes 8 muffins. Cooking time is right on - mine take 17 minutes. I add a whole can of chiles for 12 eggs. I have also tried cooked crumbled bacon rather than sausage. The mix-in possibilities are endless, and I love that they warm up perfectly in the microwave. We like to make a batch on Sunday and eat for breakfast for the week. If you want to add cheese to the recipe, add it on top for the last few minutes of cooking. Cheese in the raw egg mixture mostly disappears no matter how much you add.

This is a wonderful recipe to build on! I browned the sausage and sauteed chopped red peppers and I added green onion and cheddar cheese. I also used some heavy cream in my eggs so they got nice and fluffy. Sausage was already flavorful so I only used salt and pepper to taste. I also layered everything ...spoon full of sausage then veggies then cheese then poured in egg. This made a nice crust of the cheese and I could control how much egg (b/c I have some picky eaters)It took about 30 mins to bake. A big winner for my family!

Did anyone prepare these in cupcake liners? I prepared my muffin tin and they still stuck. I felt like I lost half of the egg entree. I added cheese but will also add milk next time around. Omit salt (too salty) and reduce garlic powder. Really enjoyed the can of green chili peppers. Agree with the other comments; it's a good dish, just needs some tweaking. Enjoy!

Personally, I would never make this recipe exactly as is...just a personal preference. However, it is a great basis and vehicle for all kinds of other ideas. You can pretty much put anything you want into these. I would definitely recommend cooking any veggies before they go in. It reduces the water content and adds much more flavor. I typically roast poblano peppers, onions, and garlic cloves before chopping it all up and adding it to the mix. I also use sliced sausage links instead of ground sausage, just a texture preference. But really, you can throw anything into this. I really want to try it with mushrooms, onions, and spinach! I've tried adding cheese a few times, but I just don't think it contributes enough extra flavor to really do much. Great general idea for a recipe!!

Even my 8 and 11 year old loved these! 

We are trying to eat more protein in our house and need something quick to eat during the morning rush. I made these according to the recipe just added a little cheese and a sprinkle of garlic and onion powder. 

I made half the batch without the chilies for the kids. Everyone was very happy and I will be making these again and again.

Quick note, next time I will sautee the onions with the sausage. Also, add the sausage to the pan and sprinkle with cheese before pouring the egg mixture on top. Next time I will add diced peppers to get more veggies in.

Like other reviewers, I found these to be a little bland. The only changes that I made, were that I used 10 eggs and about 1/4 cup whole milk, and that I used the whole can of drained green chiles. I also sauteed the onions with the sausage, once the sausage was cooked. My little man enjoyed them, but I think that next time I will add some cheese and see if that helps.
I decreased to 10 eggs, added milk and cheese. I also sauted the onion with the sausage. These needed more seasoning.

This is an excellent starter or as is! Use whatever you enjoy! Today I used vegetarian sausage, onion and sharp cheddar. It’ll be just as good as all the other hundreds of combos you could come up with!

I make it often. I've found 8 eggs along with other ingredients fills a 12 muffin pan. I don't cook pork but put 1/2 of a precooked sausage in each muffin. Shortens prep time. I mix sharp cheddar cheese in with the eggs and veggies before filling the muffin pan. My family loves them.

I read some of the other reviews and did make some changes of my own. I used a one pound package of Jimmy Dean Sage Sausage, 10 eggs, 1 cup of milk, 4 oz of green chilis and 1 cup of creamy melt cheese, and the outcome was amazing. Everyone in the house loves these and they disappear quickly.
this was a good base recipe for me. I added cheese, onions, and spinach. which made it perfect. this will be my new got to protein filled breakfast.

As is: 4 stars. It just needed something more. Second round: 10 eggs, 1/2c cheese. Made it great. Important note! Get better quality sausage. I got store brand and even though we love sausage, the aftertaste of the spices from it was kinda yuck. I'd get the next best brand above generic, at least.
Easy, very yummy. I added turkey sausage and some cheddar cheese. My family gobbled them up

Egg muffins are my new go-to breakfast on the run (used to be a hard boiled egg). So far, this is my favorite recipe. I made 6, not 12, and could heat one as I poured my coffee. All week "instant" breakfast with protein.
Did not have chili peppers, but added cheddar cheese and leftover cooked zucchini from last night's dinner. My son topped his with jarred cheese sauce. Easy and delicious!
